prs.title: fix: Add accept json headers for token request
prs.author: vincent0426
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: OAuth servers returning token responses as application/x-www-form-urlencoded instead of JSON — #1531 fixes this proactively by adding Accept: application/json to both _exchange_token and _refresh_token requests; #1511 fixes it reactively by parsing Content-Type and decoding URL-encoded response bodies on the client side. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: OAuth servers returning token responses as application/x-www-form-urlencoded instead of JSON — #1531 fixes this proactively by adding Accept: application/json to both _exchange_token and _refresh_token requests; #1511 fixes it reactively by parsing Content-Type and decoding URL-encoded response bodies on the client side. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #1531 is the simpler, more standards-aligned fix (RFC 6749 recommends requesting JSON via Accept header), covers both token exchange and refresh endpoints, includes tests in test_auth.py, and has a complete diff. #1511's diff is truncated so its full scope is unknown, and client-side content-type parsing adds complexity that becomes unnecessary once the server is asked for JSON.

prs.title: fix: `handle_sse_response` causing dangling client's read_stream
prs.author: ivanbelenky
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Client read_stream hangs indefinitely when an error occurs during request processing because the error is never forwarded to read_stream_writer. PR #1308 fixes this in the general task-exception path (post_writer spawned task); PR #1812 fixes the same gap in _handle_sse_response when the SSE stream ends without last_event_id and no reconnect occurs. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Client read_stream hangs indefinitely when an error occurs during request processing because the error is never forwarded to read_stream_writer. PR #1308 fixes this in the general task-exception path (post_writer spawned task); PR #1812 fixes the same gap in _handle_sse_response when the SSE stream ends without last_event_id and no reconnect occurs. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: PR #1812 constructs a well-formed JSONRPCError with a proper error code and descriptive message, giving callers structured error data. PR #1308 forwards raw Python exceptions to the stream, which is less structured; it also bundles an unrelated closure variable-capture fix that can be applied independently. #1812's diff is more targeted to the dangling-stream root cause and includes the SSE-specific context (last_event_id check) that #1308 does not cover.

clusters.pick_reason: PR #1812 constructs a well-formed JSONRPCError with a proper error code and descriptive message, giving callers structured error data. PR #1308 forwards raw Python exceptions to the stream, which is less structured; it also bundles an unrelated closure variable-capture fix that can be applied independently. #1812's diff is more targeted to the dangling-stream root cause and includes the SSE-specific context (last_event_id check) that #1308 does not cover.

clusters.pick_reason: #1531 is the simpler, more standards-aligned fix (RFC 6749 recommends requesting JSON via Accept header), covers both token exchange and refresh endpoints, includes tests in test_auth.py, and has a complete diff. #1511's diff is truncated so its full scope is unknown, and client-side content-type parsing adds complexity that becomes unnecessary once the server is asked for JSON.

members.title: Url encoded token response

members.reason: [llm] duplicates #1531: OAuth servers returning token responses as application/x-www-form-urlencoded instead of JSON — #1531 fixes this proactively by adding Accept: application/json to both _exchange_token and _refresh_token requests; #1511 fixes it reactively by parsing Content-Type and decoding URL-encoded response bodies on the client side.
